title: Invertible conjugate Hom action and equivariant currying
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a small site, $s:C\simeq C$ with continuous inverse, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $a:(s^{-1})^*R\simeq R$. Let $P$ be a RestrictionPresentation [def-sf-twisted-action-presentation-data] and let $T$ be TensorComparisons [lem-sf-twisted-action-tensor-comparisons]. Write $F=\sigma$, $b$ for T.sigmaTensor, and $\mathrm{ev}$ for evaluation from the tensor-Hom adjunction [def-pur-sheaf-hom, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For fixed pairs $M,N$ with invertible structure maps $\theta_M:FM\to M$ and $\theta_N:FN\to N$, put $H=\mathcal Hom_R(M,N)$ and $\gamma=\operatorname{curry}(b_{M,H}^{-1}F(\mathrm{ev}_{M,N})):FH\to\mathcal Hom_R(FM,FN)$. Define $h=\gamma\,\mathcal Hom_R(\theta_M^{-1},\theta_N):FH\to H$ in diagrammatic order. Then $h$ is invertible. Moreover, for every fixed pair $Q$ and $g:Q\to H$, writing $c=(1_M\otimes g)\mathrm{ev}_{M,N}$, the equality $F(g)h=\theta_Qg$ holds if and only if $F(c)\theta_N=b_{M,Q}(\theta_M\otimes\theta_Q)c$. This statement only concerns base-site modules and their fixed pairs; it does not assert the restriction Hom comparison.

proof.text: Apply the proved canonical Hom comparison for the translation autoequivalence. It supplies exactly invertibility of the transpose of inverse sigmaTensor followed by translated evaluation.

The map Hom(theta_M inverse,theta_N) has inverse Hom(theta_M,theta_N inverse), by bifunctoriality. Thus their composite h with the preceding transpose is invertible. Evaluation naturality shows that evaluating F(g)h after the source action equals the inverse tensor comparison followed by F of the untranspose of g, then theta_N. Evaluation of theta_Q g after the source action is exactly the diagonal-action expression. Applying these identities proves one implication; canceling the invertible source action and the tensor comparison, and using injectivity of the tensor-Hom adjunction, proves the converse. No nonzero or nonempty hypothesis enters.

theorem homPair_currying (P : RestrictionPresentation J s R a)
    (T : TensorComparisons J s R a P) (M N : Pairs (sigma J s R a)) :
    let h :=
      (SheafOfModules.tensorHomEquiv (R := R) _ _ _
        ((T.sigmaTensor M.obj.a
          (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := R) M.obj.a N.obj.a)).inv ≫
            (sigma J s R a).map (evaluationMap M.obj.a N.obj.a))) ≫
          SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := R) (pairIso M).inv (pairIso N).hom
    IsIso h ∧ ∀ (Q : Pairs (sigma J s R a))
      (g : Q.obj.a ⟶ SheafOfModules.homObj (R := R) M.obj.a N.obj.a),
      (sigma J s R a).map g ≫ h = Q.obj.str ≫ g ↔
        (sigma J s R a).map (tensorMap (𝟙 M.obj.a) g ≫
            evaluationMap M.obj.a N.obj.a) ≫ N.obj.str =
          (T.sigmaTensor M.obj.a Q.obj.a).hom ≫ tensorMap M.obj.str Q.obj.str ≫
            tensorMap (𝟙 M.obj.a) g ≫ evaluationMap M.obj.a N.obj.a
